title: Business Central: ToolTip Property Now Available on Pages

chapters.title: Introduction to tooltip feature on pages
Understanding tooltips and context for users
Reducing page size through action references and table-level tooltips
Page-level tooltips for consistency across the application
AI agents and meaningful tooltip content

features.name: ToolTip property on page objects
features.description: ToolTip and ToolTipML properties are now available directly on the page object level, allowing developers to define tooltips at the page level rather than repeatedly on individual actions.
features.status_evidence_quote: Tool tip and or tool tip ML are now available directly on business central page object.
caveats: Cannot use both ToolTip and ToolTipML simultaneously - generates an error
Actions can still override page-level tooltips if defined at action level

features.name: Action tooltip inheritance
features.description: Navigation actions can inherit tooltips from the page object when the action does not define its own tooltip, ensuring consistency across the application.
caveats: Inheritance only occurs when action does not define its own tooltip

features.name: Page-level tooltip consistency
features.description: Tooltips defined at the page level provide consistency across different areas in Business Central where the same page is referenced multiple times, reducing code duplication and ensuring uniform user experience.

features.name: AI agent tooltip support
features.description: AI agents and MCP servers within Business Central heavily rely on tooltip properties defined on pages, tables, or fields to understand page functionality and provide better assistance.
caveats: Requires meaningful tooltip content, not just static text generated by tools

features.name: Table-level tooltip inheritance
features.description: Tooltips can be defined at the table field level, and pages can inherit these tooltips without needing to redefine them on page fields, reducing page code size.
caveats: Currently not mandatory, but recommended best practice
